transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
My doctor sent me because my weight’s gotten low and everyone’s making a big fuss about it. But honestly, I feel like being lighter helps me keep up at the shop and not get slowed down.
How do you feel about the idea of gaining weight?
It scares me, honestly. If I eat something heavy—like the foods we used to make for the holidays—I start worrying right away that I’ll gain weight and lose the control I’ve worked hard to keep.
Could you tell me your current height and weight?
I don’t know the exact numbers offhand. My doctor says my weight has dropped very low, but I feel like being lighter helps me keep up at the shop without getting slowed down.
Have your menstrual periods stopped or become irregular since your weight dropped?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping track of that closely.
When you look at your body, do you see yourself as being too fat or overweight?

I don’t know if I’d say “too fat,” exactly, but when I look at myself, I worry about gaining. If I eat heavier food, especially holiday-type foods, I feel like I’m losing the control I’ve worked hard to keep.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating to prevent weight gain?
No, I don’t make myself vomit after I eat.
When was the last time you had a menstrual period?
I honestly couldn’t tell you. I haven’t been paying attention to the dates.
Do you strictly limit how much food you eat each day to keep your weight down?
Yes. On days I’m in the workshop, I usually just have tea and maybe a few careful bites of something. Stopping for a proper meal feels unnecessary, and it throws off the control I have over the day.
Do you see yourself as being underweight right now, or does your body look normal to you?
I think I look normal. My husband and the apprentices say I’m too thin, but I’m fine. They’re mistaking discipline for something being wrong.
Do you exercise excessively or feel compelled to work out to burn calories and keep your weight down?
I’m not sure what you’d count as excessive. I’m on my feet a lot with my work, but I don’t set aside time to work out or anything.
Do you use laxatives, water pills, or diet pills to try to control your weight?
I’m not really sure what you mean by water pills. I haven’t noticed needing anything like that.
Have you had any menstrual bleeding at all over the past few months?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really kept track of that.
Do you take laxatives to help manage or reduce your weight?
I don’t think so. I haven’t been taking anything specifically to reduce my weight.
Are you currently taking any birth control pills or hormone treatments?
I don’t think I’m taking anything like that right now.
Did your doctor tell you your exact body mass index (BMI) or by how much your weight is below normal?

They didn’t give me an exact BMI. They just said my weight had gotten very low and sent me here. Everyone’s making a fuss, but honestly, being lighter helps me keep up at the shop without feeling slowed down.
Do you take any diet pills or appetite suppressants to help keep your weight down?
No, I’m not taking diet pills or anything to suppress my appetite.
Do you have a rough idea of how much weight you have lost recently?

I don’t know the exact amount. My doctor just said my weight had dropped very low and sent me here. I know everyone’s worried, but I feel like being lighter helps me keep up at the shop without getting slowed down.
Have you set a specific weight limit or maximum weight for yourself that you feel you must stay below?

I don’t have a number written down, but I do feel like I have to keep my weight from going up. If I eat something heavy, especially holiday foods we used to make, I worry right away that I’ll gain and lose the control I’ve worked hard to keep.
Have you already gone through menopause?
I’m not really sure what you mean by that.
How old are you?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with significant self-induced food restriction, intense fear of weight gain, and body image distortion (perceiving her significantly low weight as normal and mistaking undernutrition for discipline). However, full criteria for typical anorexia nervosa (F50.0) are not met due to the absence of demonstrable amenorrhea/endocrine disturbance applicable to her postmenopausal age (59 years old) and lack of precise documented BMI/weight loss parameters, fulfilling the diagnosis of atypical anorexia nervosa.

confirmed_symptoms: Intense fear of weight gain and losing control over weight
Deliberate dietary restriction (consuming only tea and minimal bites of food)
Distorted body image (minimization of low weight, viewing emaciation as normal/discipline)
Low weight acknowledged by medical provider and family

additional_requirements: Absence of one or more core criteria of F50.0 (amenorrhea criterion unfulfilled/not assessable in a 59-year-old female)
